text.p: These are the leading stories in the Albanian press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
KOHA JONE

- OSCE special envoy Franz Vranitzky has a last chance to put an end to a growing political crisis sparked after the Democratic Party had its draft of a new electoral law passed by the Democrat-dominated parliament.
- An editorial accuses President Sali Berisha of provoking an insurrection, saying his attempts to ignore a broad-based government of national reconciliation may plunge the country into a civil war.

- National Intelligence Service (Shik) officers and collaborators operating in the southern town of Skrapar have been the target of violence from enraged residents after a list with their names was published.
GAZETA SHQIPTARE
- Italian officials could not identify the corpse of a woman who was one of numerous Albanians who drowned after their ship sank after a collision with an Italian frigate.
- A Greek citizen was killed and two Albanians were wounded as they were caught up in the fight between two gangs which in the southern town of Vlore.
- Zef Mazi, Albania's representative at the OSCE, said the European security body was not considering a possible withdrawal of the multinational protection force.
ALBANIA

- Two women waiting to receive their social benefits at the municipality of Berat in southern Albania were killed by a gunman who started shooting in the air but could not control his weapon which was later directed against the crowd.
- President Berisha has annulled a decree to dissolve parliament.
- Parliament approved the law for private and public radios and televisions.
ZERI I POPULLIT
- OSCE envoy Franz Vranitzky has appealed for consensus among parties although a law that was expected to be agreed by all parties was rammed through parliament by the Democrats.
-Socialist Party leader Fatos Nano said his party would not react with threats to their rival Democrats over the passage of an election law. He added they hoped the situation would return to normal.
INDIPENDENT
- Unknown people used tear gas near a primary school in Tirana.
- Eduard Dervishi, the secretary-general of Albanian Soccer Federation, has been sacked. He is abroad.
- President Sali Berisha formed an electoral alliance called the Union for Democracy, bringing together five rightist parties.
- The political committee of an international military mission decided that the Alba multinational force will cooperate with the OSCE during elections expected on June 29, the paper says.
